summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 (only the oldest videos reached 400-680). The best videos are short 'X doesn't do what you think, it actually does Y' explainers about robots and sound sensors, with the clap switch and line-follower robots earning the most likes, saves and shares. Question-style titles like 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' got zero Instagram posts and almost no views anywhere, and the newest videos have lower reach, so quality of topic and hook matters more than posting volume.
winningPattern: Relatable robot or sound-sensor subject (clap switch, gyro robot, line follower, IR obstacle robot, mic) + a surprising contrast or 'myth-bust' hook ('X doesn't do Y, it only does Z' or 'Without X this robot falls') + short Hinglish title with one emoji and #shorts + posted on Instagram Reels first. Shares come from curiosity or 'did you know' facts (UV sensor in clouds, soil sensor), saves from clear how-it-works explainers that makers want to revisit.
doMore: Post every video on Instagram Reels first, then YouTube Shorts, since IG gives 10-50x more views
Make robot and clap-switch style series: a demo with a visible 'before/after' result in the first 2 seconds
Use contrast hooks: 'X doesn't do Y, it does Z' or 'Without X, this fails'
Add a save-worthy ending, like a one-line circuit tip or 'save this for your next project', to lift saves
Make a follow-up to winners (clap switch part 3, gyro robot balance, line follower with IR) and test a YouTube-specific title with the same topic in English
stopDoing: Generic 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' question titles for everyday objects (taps, doors, street lights, smoke alarms)
Publishing only on YouTube with no Instagram version
Narrow spec-sheet topics (geophone, TDS meter, CO2, geyser thermocouple) that got under 500 views and almost no engagement
